scope: Sealed fly-neural results already in this repository, read and checked; none re-run. Neural-model validation only: no controller, no behavioural verdict, no original individual.

criteria.claim: Development: everything reported, nothing judged
Learning helps: after relocation the full subject reaches criterion sooner than one that cannot learn
and sooner than the existing connectome mechanism (v1 on the dense code)
and eats more per visit than the existing connectome mechanism
It reverses faster than the merged rule on the same code, which can only depress
At least 80% of full subjects reach criterion after all three reversals
After 100 visits elsewhere the trained site is still preferred more than by a subject that never learned
with at least 60% of the first 5 probe visits to it on average
Dopamine is needed: silencing it removes the gain
Dopamine must follow the meal: uncoupled from it, the gain goes
The code matters: v2 on the dense code relearns more slowly
The antennal-lobe change matters: v2 on the threshold-only code relearns more slowly

Persistence: every full subject restored from its checkpoint after each block makes exactly the choices it makes uninterrupted; the checkpoints chain by hash; the state holds as many numbers after every block
The same for ECHO's mushroom body
No degradation: over 12 relocations the full subject's trials to criterion in the last four blocks are on average at most 2 visits more than in the first four
Exploratory: ECHO's mushroom body, the bookkeeping heuristic, random codes, no dopamine threshold and a random forager, on every metric
Development: everything reported, nothing judged
Safety: every neural run completes its 30 s without being stopped
and ECHO decides at most 1% of its samples (fallbacks)
Escape is produced, not only predicted: at least 90% of neural-selected escape commands in the looms become escapes
Feeding is produced: at least 90% of neural-selected feeding commands on the fruit become feeding bouts
Discrimination in closed loop: the selected readout escapes harmless objects no more often than the merged one
and still escapes at least 75% of the threats that begin while it is perched
Exploratory: every arm against ECHO alone on escapes, false alarms, feeding time and meals

primary: on every held-out condition, the reduced circuit's mean MN9 rate is within the readout tolerance of the whole brain's (2% of the whole brain's rate or 1 Hz, whichever is larger), under the same random draws
at least min_exact_share of held-out trials equal the whole brain's spike counts on every kept neuron
every held-out trial in which no neuron outside the cut spikes is exact (the cut's exactness argument holds)
Development: every arm's indices (3 subjects; nothing judged)
Precondition: each odour reaches the readout MBONs before training (fixed weights, sparse code)
Precondition: each odour reaches the readout MBONs before training
With rule v2 on the sparse code, the paired odour's response falls more than the unpaired one's, in every subject, by at least 0.10 on average
The same on the second held-out pair
Fixed weights learn less
Fixed weights learn less
Silencing the DANs abolishes it
Silencing the DANs abolishes it
It depends on which odour was rewarded: shuffling rewards within a phase removes it
Shuffling rewards removes it
v2 on the sparse code is more odour-specific than the merged mechanism (v1 on the dense code)
More odour-specific than the merged mechanism
It spares the unpaired odour more than the merged mechanism does (less nonspecific depression of B)
It spares the unpaired odour more
The memory survives an unrelated, unrewarded odour: the index after the distractor is negative in every subject and at least half the acquisition index on average
Unrewarded re-exposure to A extinguishes the memory: A's response recovers in every subject
and recovers more than under the merged rule, which can only depress
Reversal: after B is rewarded and A not, B's response falls below A's in every subject
With a 200 ms gap between odour and reward, the eligibility trace carries the association
The dopamine threshold matters: counting odour-evoked PAM activity as reward makes learning less specific
The sparse code matters: rule v2 on the dense code is less specific
The antennal-lobe change matters beyond sparseness: rule v2 on the threshold-only code is less specific
Exploratory: rule v2 with PN->KC targets permuted; generalization to Asim; every arm's indices
Exploratory: every arm's indices
The merged readout (v1 mapping, any spike) still over-fires on the held-out battery: its false alarms per simulated minute are at least 5
The selected readout cuts false alarms per minute by at least 80% from the merged readout
without an unacceptable rise in misses: recall at least 0.75 and no more than 0.10 below the merged readout's

notRun: A behavioural comparison of a connectome-driven research fly against the organism under the bench's protocol: not run. The whole-brain model costs 3.2731 wall seconds per simulated second (docs/benchmarks/fly-neural/adaptive/feeding-reduced-v783-heldout.json, on the machine it names), so one 2-hour run would take about 6.5 hours, and a protocol needs hundreds.
Re-running any fly-neural experiment: not run here; their seals and criteria are read as reference cases.
limits: A criterion passing means a model output met a threshold against a published observation, not that the model is the fly's nervous system.
FAFB v783 and BANC v888 are different animals; their results are listed apart and never pooled.
Resources were measured on the machines each result names; they are not comparable across results run on different hardware.
